title: Mineral Wells and the Crazy Water Crystals transcription programs
summary: Weekly he and a small crew went to Mineral Wells to cut 16-inch discs for XEPN, with an accordion, organ effects and no vocals so ads could be talked over the music.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: That's very interesting. The next thing I'd like to discuss is your experience with the border stations. All right.
Somebody from Mineral Wells, what was that man's name? What was his name?
Well, the name I thought last night was Fincher. But he was around Asheville that he promoted the Crazy Water Crystals. But I never associated him with Mineral Wells.

I thought it was Tom something. I don't think it's a shame person. I don't know. Somebody who had stock or owned stock in Mineral Wells with Crazy Water Crystals in Mineral Wells, Texas. That's where the company first started and had its home office.
It could be that the company had an eastern representative in Asheville who was Fincher, and then someone else did its Texas work.

But Mineral Wells has that crazy water. There's a big spring there and all. It started off with that old spring and then he started bottling this crazy water and selling it. And everybody would go to that mineral, kind of a spa there in Mineral Wells. That's the name of the town, Mineral Wells. That's where the whole thing came from, Crazy Water. And a little select crew, once again our same ever-loving three, and two violinists went with us. And it seems to me we picked up another bass player or somebody else downtown. There was enmity in the band between some of the others and we didn't want them. We'd pick out our old stall where it's Faithful's. And one night a week we'd go over to Mineral Wells. We'd leave in the afternoon and get there around six. And he had a quantity of big tape, no, I mean big discs. This is back in 37, 36, 37. Big 15 minute 16 inch discs. And slap these discs on and we'd start playing. And by the time, sometimes during the play the guy would make out the program while we were playing, just slap down a number there in the key and that's it. We're off. And then he'd point to somebody, we'd get up there and play solos, or I had an accordion and piano. Also they had an organ in the studio. And for the evening programs we'd want some lullaby, some organ. I couldn't play the foot, but at all the organ. I didn't have any idea about how to play the footwork. But they had this bass, it would bow the bass to be as if it were organ music. Bowed bass you see, and the other parts of the organ played and nobody would know the difference. And the violets playing dreamy, dreamy music. One of the radio programs were for night, dreamy lullabies for going to sleep. Ten o'clock. We used to hear them sometimes on XCPN. And they would tone down the music then and put in an ad. And then bring out the music and then tone it down and put in another ad, constantly selling all kinds of stuff.

Oh yes. Then in the noonday program we would be a little bit free. We didn't have any vocals and everything was instrumental. So they could do this. Whew. Also, they thought if we didn't have any vocals there would be no identification with the group. But it was anybody with any knowledge of music could identify at once, that banjo especially. This is Marvin Montgomery, no doubt. And the tunes, the same arrangements and everything. There we go.
